text:
alice (sre): :rotating_light: paging ops: seeing p95/p99 spikes for streaming paths since ~09:04UTC, stalls and chunking delays reported by multiple customers

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2935 - Streaming chunking + proxy timeouts (severity: P1) - paging oncall@#incidents

mike (support): getting a bunch of customer reports: widgets app sees long pauses then a big chunk, clients show timeouts at ~30s. They say websocket sessions hang and SSE clients show large buffered intervals.

jane (platform): logs look like the proxy is queuing write buffers. p95 for streaming-response has jumped from 120ms -> 2.4s, p99 -> 18s. Backend model latency looks fine.

alice (sre): suspected path: proxy -> connection write blocked -> keepalive/epoll backlog -> client backpressure -> worker threads hit queue limits -> timeouts. Need to confirm if it's proxy or upstream.

mike (support): one customer provided a client trace:

```
Client: websocket send
Server: accepts conn
09:03:12 first chunk
09:03:12.1 chunk 2
09:03:45 no chunk for 30s
09:04:15 huge buffered chunk delivered
Client: socket close
```

jane (platform): reproduced in staging by firing many concurrent low-throughput streaming clients. Proxy accumulates buffered writes when consumers read slowly.

alice (sre): immediate mitigation options? Thoughts: 1) enable aggressive chunk flush (force smaller chunks) on proxy 2) short circuit to non-streaming endpoint for affected customers 3) rate-limit slow-consumers at edge 4) temporarily scale proxy workers / increase epoll backlog.

mike (support): customers want ETA and mitigation. Which option is fastest?

jane (platform): fastest deploy is a runtime toggle: set PROXY_STREAM_FLUSH_MS=250 and reduce max write buffer to 64KB. That's a config flip we can roll via console in ~5m and revert. Risk: may increase CPU due to more writes.

alice (sre): roll plan: canary to 5% of proxy fleet in us-west then 30m monitor p95/p99 and error rates. If we see increased CPU but reduced tail latency, continue. If errors spike, rollback.

oncall-bot: @oncall alice (sre) acknowledged the incident.

mike (support): pinging affected customers with a short note that we're investigating and applying mitigation in ~10m.

alice (sre): executing console change now. Rolling to canary group: proxy-frontend-usw-01..05.

deploy-bot: config-update applied to proxy-frontend-usw-01..05 by alice (sre) at 09:12UTC.

jane (platform): canary metrics: p95 from 2.4s -> 0.28s, p99 from 18s -> 1.6s on canary. CPU bump +8% on those nodes. No increase in 5xx observed.

alice (sre): good. expanding to 40% of prod fleet. continuing to monitor. Notifying support to hold customer comms pending next update.

mike (support): update sent to customers: short note + plugging in ETA for wide mitigation.

jane (platform): noticing proxy keepalive counters rising (many clients with low read throughput) — we should add a slow-consumer enforcement in the longer term. Filing follow-up runbook item.

alice (sre): mid-term mitigations to schedule: - implement slow-consumer eviction in proxy (configurable threshold), - add per-connection write-window accounting, - surface per-client backpressure metrics to console.

mike (support): any impact on billing or data loss? customers asking.

jane (platform): no data loss observed. Some long-poll clients disconnected and retried; clients that cannot tolerate stalls might see dropped responses and will need retries. Billing unaffected.

alice (sre): widening change to 100% now.

deploy-bot: config-update applied to proxy-frontend-usw-* by alice (sre) at 09:21UTC.

jane (platform): post-roll p95: 0.22s, p99: 1.1s globally. Error rate steady. Proxy CPU +6% across fleet.

oncall-bot: INC-2935 status -> Mitigated (config toggle).

mike (support): sending final customer note: we applied temporary chunk flush/tuning to mitigate streaming stalls. Engineering will follow up on permanent fixes.

alice (sre): postmortem tasks created: PMT-832 (slow-consumer eviction), INF-129 (per-conn metrics), DOCS-452 (runbook for streaming outages).

jane (platform): root cause hypothesis: large fraction of clients with poor consumption rates created a buildup in proxy write buffers, exposing an unbounded write-batch behavior in our streaming path which amplified tail latency and triggered proxy timeouts.

alice (sre): tagging as handoff to eng-runtime for long-term fixes. Oncall handing back to platform.

oncall-bot: Handoff: oncall incident owner alice (sre) -> assignee: eng-runtime. Next update due EOD.

mike (support): closing comm loop. Thanks all. :clap:

alice (sre): final notes: keep an eye on related metrics for next 48h: streaming_p95_ms, streaming_p99_ms, proxy_write_queue_depth, slow_consumer_count. If any regresses, reopen INC-2935.
